original_question: Given a modulus of continuity ω, construct a compact set K such that the Green function g_{C\K} for the complement C\K with pole at infinity has modulus of continuity comparable to ω. More precisely, require the modulus ω(g_{C\K},·) to be similar to ω, for example by weak equivalence in the sense that there exist constants C1,C2>0 such that C1·ω(δ) ≤ ω(g_{C\K},δ) ≤ C2·ω(δ) for all sufficiently small positive δ.
target_in_paper: Section 2, Problem 1: "Given modulus of continuity ω, find a compact set K such that the modulus of continuity ω(g_{C\setminus K},·) is similar to ω."
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper’s actual target as the inverse modulus-of-continuity problem for the Green function g_{C\setminus K} with pole at infinity: given a modulus of continuity ω, choose a compact set K so that the modulus of continuity of g_{C\setminus K} matches ω up to comparison constants for small scales. The weak-equivalence inequality you wrote is exactly one of the two notions of "similarity" explicitly mentioned in the paper.
missing_details: The paper’s ambient setting is the complex plane: K is a compact subset of C, not necessarily of R.
Section 2 imposes the standing assumption that K is regular with respect to the Dirichlet problem, so that g_{C\setminus K} is continuous throughout C.
To make the question stand-alone, the modulus of continuity ω(g_{C\setminus K},δ) should be defined explicitly, e.g. as sup{|g_{C\setminus K}(z)-g_{C\setminus K}(w)| : |z-w|≤δ}.

The paper’s official wording allows two meanings of "similar": either coincidence of the values of the two moduli on some null sequence, or weak equivalence via constants C1,C2>0 for all sufficiently small δ>0. Your draft includes only the second option.

The paper’s Problem 1 concerns the modulus of continuity itself; the stronger pointwise estimate C1ω(dist(z,K))≤g_{C\setminus K}(z)≤C2ω(dist(z,K)) is a separate neighboring statement (Problem 2) and should not be merged into the official formulation.
No extra restriction such as K⊂R or a Hölder form ω(δ)=δ^α should be built into the refined question; those belong to the separate special-case Problem 3.

It is implicit that K must be a compact set for which the Green function of C\setminus K with pole at infinity is defined; the paper handles this through its standing Green-function notation and regularity assumption.
refined_question: Given a modulus of continuity ω, find a compact set K⊂C, regular with respect to the Dirichlet problem, such that the Green function g_{C\setminus K} of C\setminus K with pole at infinity is continuous on C and has modulus of continuity similar to ω; that is, with ω(g_{C\setminus K},δ):=sup{|g_{C\setminus K}(z)-g_{C\setminus K}(w)|:|z-w|≤δ}, require that as δ↓0 either ω(g_{C\setminus K},·) and ω coincide on some null sequence, or, in the weak-equivalence sense spelled out in the paper, there exist constants C1,C2>0 such that C1ω(δ)≤ω(g_{C\setminus K},δ)≤C2ω(δ) for all sufficiently small positive δ.
justification: The draft is targeting Section 2, Problem 1 (p. 15), not the stronger Section 2, Problem 2 or the special Hölder-on-the-line Section 2, Problem 3 (p. 16). The paper’s exact formulation asks for a compact set K whose Green-function modulus of continuity is "similar" to a prescribed modulus ω, and it immediately explains that this similarity may mean either coincidence on a null sequence or weak equivalence by two-sided constants for sufficiently small δ (Section 2, Problem 1, p. 15). The standing assumptions for this section are that K is regular with respect to the Dirichlet problem, so g_{C\setminus K} is continuous throughout C (Section 2, opening paragraph, p. 15), and the notation g_{C\setminus K} refers to the Green function for C\setminus K with pole at infinity (Section 1.1, p. 14). The sentence after Problem 1 only suggests that the Cantor-type sets K(γ) from [12] may be candidates; it does not make that restriction part of the official problem (Section 2, p. 15).
